decision_reason: Knoten is a documented USGS planetary CSM library distributed through conda-forge with versioned 0.4.0 release and current USGS installation/tutorial documentation. Its current public canonical repository is active, and the initial 2018 public source already carried the Unlicense; the current CC0 file supplements that worldwide grant.

government_provenance.note: Current first-party USGS Astrogeology documentation identifies Knoten as a component of its Community Sensor Model (CSM) software stack and links dedicated Knoten use tutorials.

public_source.note: The assigned Code.USGS project is publicly accessible and its current DOI-USGS GitHub canonical repository is public without credentials; current source was pushed in June 2026.

eligible_license.note: Current LICENSE.md makes a worldwide CC0 dedication; the initial public repository commit in November 2018 included an Unlicense dedication, so the first eligible source predates the later CC0 template.

primary_evidence.note: USGS provides a product-specific installation and execution tutorial using Knoten 0.4; the official software release process lists Knoten and its GitHub/conda-forge distribution.

product_identity: Knoten, a Python geospatial/sensor-exploitation library that uses Python-wrapped Community Sensor Models for planetary camera operations, coordinate conversion, and testing.
agency: U.S. Geological Survey, Astrogeology Science Center
geography: United States federal agency; Astrogeology Science Center, Flagstaff, Arizona
license: Unlicense (worldwide public-domain dedication) in the initial 2018 source; current repository also contains a CC0-1.0 worldwide dedication
status_note: The first public source commit (2018-11-29) included the Unlicense text; the separate 2022 CC0 migration is not used to backdate the first grant. USGS documentation currently provides Knoten 0.4 installation and use guidance, the USGS general release workflow lists Knoten, and DOI-USGS/knoten has substantive 2026 source activity. The README notes that some CSM instrument implementations remain short of production readiness, but the library itself is an officially distributed reusable tool.

decision_reason: This repository is the Hugo source and content for the USGS Planetary Analysis Ready Data documentation portal, not the underlying STAC API, data service, or a distinct software tool. The live site is user documentation for those separate services. Treating the documentation source as the service implementation would transfer the service's deployment/use evidence to the wrong product, so this row fails the independent product-identity/notability gate.

government_provenance.note: The first-party site explicitly identifies itself as the USGS Astrogeology Science Center's ARD documentation portal; its Edit page link points to the canonical DOI-USGS/planetary-ard source.

public_source.note: The linked canonical public repository exposes the static-site source/content without credentials; the assigned Code.USGS project contains Hugo content/layout/theme files and no ARD API implementation.

eligible_license.note: The actual LICENSE.md includes a worldwide CC0 1.0 waiver for the authors' work. Its human-readable template summary names another project, but the operative grant is for this project/work.

primary_evidence.note: The first-party portal describes this exact repository's output as tutorials, examples, accuracy documentation, and links to the separately hosted USGS ARD API/data portal.

product_identity: Analysis Ready Data Documentation: a Hugo static documentation/content site for the separate USGS planetary ARD API and data portal; not the API, catalog server, or an independently reusable software product.
agency: U.S. Geological Survey, Astrogeology Science Center
geography: United States federal agency; Astrogeology Science Center, Flagstaff, Arizona
license: CC0-1.0 Universal (worldwide dedication for repository-authored site source/content)
status_note: The live portal currently resolves and its page-edit control links to DOI-USGS/planetary-ard, which has recent site-source activity. decision_reason: Planetary I/O (PLIO) is an officially documented and distributed Python library for planetary-data input/output. USGS software documentation gives user installation/reference guidance, the current public DOI-USGS repository released version 1.6.3 in April 2026, and the first verified global public-domain grant is the Unlicense added to the public source in January 2019.

government_provenance.note: The official USGS Astrogeology release workflow explicitly lists PLIO among its software products; USGS-hosted manuals document the package.

public_source.note: The assigned USGS GitLab project is public and links to the current public DOI-USGS/plio canonical source, which is actively maintained.

eligible_license.note: Current LICENSE.md states a worldwide CC0 dedication; the first public repository license was an Unlicense in 2019, a clear worldwide public-domain grant. Third-party dependency licenses are separately documented.

primary_evidence.note: First-party USGS user documentation identifies PLIO, documents conda and setup.py installation, and links its reference/user guides; the official GitHub release history shows current release 1.6.3.

product_identity: Planetary I/O (PLIO), a Python library of reusable input/output utilities for planetary datasets, geospatial data, and planetary tool formats.

The initial eligible Unlicense text entered the public repository on 2019-01-02; the older repository creation date (2016) is not treated as a license date.

decision_reason: PyHAT is a notable USGS spectroscopy analysis library/GUI with an official 2025 user guide and a versioned 0.1.2 release. The original public source carried the Unlicense in 2016, but the current repository's LICENSE.md states that the software has not received final USGS approval and that CC0 will be applied only after review/approval. This conflicts with its current CC0 claim and does not establish an eligible grant for all current code; hold for agency/maintainer clarification of present scope.

government_provenance.note: The official USGS Open-File Report identifies PyHAT as a USGS-developed tool, names the Astrogeology Science Center and documents the exact 0.1.2 product; it also describes NASA funding and USGS support.

public_source.note: The assigned Code.USGS repository, its 0.1.2 release, and source files are publicly viewable without credentials; the official user guide links this exact repository.

eligible_license.note: The current LICENSE.md says the software has not received final USGS approval and that the following CC0 license will be applied upon approval, so the included CC0 legal text is conditional. A historical Unlicense grant exists in the original 2016 source, but the current scope across post-2016 contributions is unclear.

primary_evidence.note: USGS Open-File Report 2025-1038 is a product-specific user guide for PyHAT 0.1.2 and provides installation, support, documentation, capabilities, and example workflows.

product_identity: Python Hyperspectral Analysis Tool (PyHAT), a Python library and GUI for spectroscopy data preprocessing, analysis, machine learning, and visualization.

status_note: The original source's 2016 commit contains an Unlicense; the source later changed to a provisional/conditional license, including the 2023 "software not yet approved" update. USGS's 2025 Open-File Report is for version 0.1.2, links the current Code.USGS repository, and documents installation and community support. Historical licensed code exists, but that alone does not prove a license for all current repository content.
